nodes.question: What catalytic principle is suggested for fostering resilient, low-carbon construction?
nodes.answer: Leveraging circular economy principles is suggested for fostering resilient, low-carbon construction.
nodes.paragraph: Demand-side measures, including sustainable construction practices, recycling, and green procurement policies, further drive industry-wide adoption of low-carbon solutions. Summary Through a systems-thinking approach, this paper advocates for reducing material intensity across all stages of production and design, leveraging circular economy principles, and fostering resilient, low-carbon construction. Highlight - ing global initiatives, the study offers actionable insights for achieving net-zero targets in the cement industry by aligning stakeholders across the value chain to drive climate action while promoting equity, environmental justice, and economic sustainability. Keywords Cement industry decarbonization Carbon capture and storage Supplementary cementitious materials Sustainable construction practices Policy frameworks Circular economyAccepted: 18 February 2025 The Author(s) 2025Towards a Net Zero Cement: Strategic Policies and Systems Thinking for a Low-Carbon Future Sanjeev Kumar1 Ankita Gangotra2 Michael Barnard3 1 3 Current Sustainable/Renewable Energy Reports (2025) 12:5 developed for carbon neutrality in the cement sector which all present a multifaceted approach including integrating supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), alternative fuels, energy efficiency, carbon capture technologies, and innovative cement formulations, alongside sustainable con - struction practices to drastically reduce the sector S carbon footprint and align with global climate objectives [ 2 5].

nodes.question: By what percentage did circularity increase in old buildings due to the adoption of biocompatible materials and regenerative design, according to Honarvar et al. (2022)?
nodes.answer: Circularity increased by 27% in old buildings.
nodes.paragraph: 2013; Pe a et al. 2021; Sazdovski et al. 2021), effectively con- tributing to more efficient use of resources and environmen- tal protection, in different sectors (Toniolo et al. 2019). In recent years, several studies have shown the positive inter - action between LCA and circular economy. By applying the LCA methodology in the construction industry, Honar - var et al. (2022) showed an increase in circularity of 27% in old buildings and 3% in new ones due to the adoption of biocompatible materials and regenerative design. Like- wise, Bj rnbet and Vild sen S (2021) study on a Norwegian manufacturer revealed that LCA is a suitable methodology for the development of circular business models as it pro- vides quantified results about the environmental impacts of circular strategies, limiting the risk of problem shifting and considering multiple environmental impact categories. On the other hand, the use of the LCA method enabled Ncube et al. (2022) to carry out comparative assessments between linear and circular production within the supply chain of Italian extra virgin olive oil, leading to the definition of proper circular strategies to reduce environmental footprints in this sector.
